name: Anantara Kihavah Maldives Villas
positioning: Private-island villa resort in the Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, with an overwater observatory, an underwater restaurant and an overwater spa
best_for: Travelers who want to snorkel with manta rays near Hanifaru Bay
Couples who want a private-pool villa on the beach or over the water
Families who want a kids' club and multi-bedroom residences

facts.text: Anantara Kihavah is a private island in the Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
A house reef surrounds the island.
Manta ray season at Hanifaru Bay runs from May to November.
Guests can stargaze at SKY through the Indian Ocean's most powerful telescope.
Villas sit on sandy shores or over the water, each with its own pool and a swinging daybed.
Villas come with Villa Host service.
Residences have two to four bedrooms, each with an ensuite.
The overwater spa has floor-to-ceiling glass windows and offers therapies rooted in Ayurvedic tradition, sound healing and energy healing.
Snorkeling equipment, life jackets and kayaks are complimentary.
The resort has a dive centre, a padel court, a tennis court and a water sports centre.
At SEA, daytime brings turtles, butterflyfish, unicorn fish and jackfish, while dinner attracts lionfish, reef sharks, moray eels and sting rays.

highlights.text: SKY is the Maldives' first overwater observatory.
The resort is minutes away from Hanifaru Bay, home to the world's largest gatherings of manta rays.
At the overwater spa, marine life glides beneath the treatment bed.
Villa bathtubs either have glass bottoms or are surrounded by reflection ponds.
SEA is an underwater restaurant, set beneath the ocean.

considerations.text: The resort is a 35-minute seaplane journey from Male International Airport.
Unauthorised drones are prohibited on the resort premises; there is a professional photography and videography studio on site.
The Thiththi Boli Kids' Club is for children aged 4 to 12.
